providers.title: Evaluations keep distances
providers.scope: In the Lipschitz-free space F(M) of a pointed metric space, |delta_x - delta_y| = d(x, y).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Linearization of Lipschitz maps
providers.scope: A pointed Lambda-Lipschitz map u between pointed metric spaces induces exactly one bounded linear operator between the free spaces with delta_x -> delta_(u(x)); its norm is at most Lambda.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: From a dense set to compact sets
providers.scope: If bounded operators S_m on a Banach space have norms at most lambda and S_m v -> v on a dense set, then S_m -> Id uniformly on every compact set.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The free space of a bounded countable space with distances at least 1
providers.scope: For a countable pointed metric space N with distances >= 1 and diameter <= B, c -> sum c_x delta_x is a linear bijection of l_1(N minus o) onto F(N) with (1/2)|c|_1 <= |Jc| <= B|c|_1, and F(N) has 2B-BAP.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A uniformly discrete space whose free space has AP and not BAP
providers.scope: There is a countable pointed metric space M with distances >= 1 such that F(M) has the approximation property and has lambda-BAP for no lambda. Proved in the lesson on the wedge from the theorem on blocks. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Norms on l_1 without the metric approximation property
providers.scope: For every integer p >= 1 the real space l_1 has a norm with (1/2)|c|_1 <= |c|_p <= B_p |c|_1, B_p = 300p^2 + 150p + 5, that has 2B_p-BAP and not p-BAP. For p = 1 it fails the metric approximation property. No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The approximation property of a wedge
providers.scope: If the free space of each of countably many pointed metric spaces has the bounded approximation property (with constants that may be unbounded), the free space of their wedge has the approximation property.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Linearization of maps into a Banach space
providers.scope: A Lambda-Lipschitz map gamma from a pointed metric space M to a Banach space X with gamma(o) = 0 extends to exactly one bounded linear operator T from F(M) to X with T delta_x = gamma(x); its norm is at most Lambda.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: A space with AP that is not approximable
providers.scope: Assume (K) (a theorem of Kalton on nets; not proved in the programme). If M is countable with distances >= 1 and F(M) fails BAP, then F(M) is not approximable.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Balls in permutation multigraphs are trees
providers.scope: For Delta/2 independent uniform permutations of N vertices and two different vertices, the balls of radius r around them are disjoint tree balls with probability at least 1 - C^2/(N - C), C = 2(1 + Delta + ... + Delta^(r+1)).
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Colored regular multigraphs with a colored tree limit
providers.scope: For even Delta >= 4 and k >= 1 there is a sequence of finite Delta-regular multigraphs with vertex colors in 1..k such that for every r and every type of colored ball of radius r the fraction of vertices with this type converges to its probability in the Delta-regular tree with independent uniform colors.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The geometry of the block
providers.scope: The block M_p: an integer-valued metric with diameter <= B_p; labels are 1-Lipschitz for the sup norm; every source vertex has distance R to its anchor and at least R to all anchors; closed balls of radius 2L have at most Q points; every label has at most H coordinates below D.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The signed measures of an operator
providers.scope: An operator on F(M_p) with range in the span of finitely many evaluations, norm <= 2p and anchor errors < 1 defines signed measures mu_x of mass 1 with the affine pairing, total variation <= 1 + 4pB and bump integral >= 3L/4.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Long matched walks are rare
providers.scope: For a finite set S of states and n >= 1, the fraction of vertices of G_m at which a matched walk of length n starts has limsup at most |S| (H/k) (Delta Q H / k)^n.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Exceptional directions
providers.scope: For an incidence e from x to y and states j, j' with x, j compatible, y, j' compatible and d(j, j') <= 2L: e is exceptional at (x, j) or its reverse is exceptional at (y, j').
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: Extension of real Lipschitz functions from a finite set
providers.scope: For 1-Lipschitz data v on a finite subset P of a metric space with values in [-L, L], z -> min over j of (v(j) + d(z, j)), cut off at L and -L, is a 1-Lipschitz extension with values in [-L, L].
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review

providers.title: The anchor obstruction
providers.scope: For every integer p >= 1, every bounded linear operator T_0 of finite rank on F(M_p) with norm <= p has |T_0 delta_a - delta_a| >= 1/2 for some anchor a. (Exercise 7.4: even >= 150p^2 + 7p.) No hypothesis.
providers.status: proof written in the course; self-checked by the writing AI; no independent review
